text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary deploy 2024-11-?? (canary-42) - 10x increase in 5xx and a pattern of empty request bodies detected. Impact: some hosted API requests failing. Paging eng-oncall. :rotating_light:

olivia_oncall: Saw it. Investigating now. Which region?

incident-bot: Metrics: us-west-2 canary pool. Error rate jumped from 0.3% -> 12% at 09:58 UTC. Sample logs show repeated requests with Content-Length: 0 followed by proxy 502.

sam_sre: Is this traffic actually routed to canary or is it a proxy returning after a TCP reset? Can someone paste a sample request/resp?

jessica_eng: grabbing logs from sidecar. Looks like requests keep retrying and hit an empty body on the model service. Suspect sidecar->runtime handshake drop.

nina_infra: Confirmed. I see the sidecar health probes flapping on a subset of canary nodes. kube events show Liveness probe restarts around the same time.

olivia_oncall: Impact? Any customers on dedicated capacity?

matt_prodops: No dedicated customers affected, this is hosted API canary only. Some PLG users on us-west may see increased 5xx. CS notified.

jessica_eng: quick dump of the failing request header (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Content-Length: 0
User-Agent: rwl-client/1.2.0
X-Model: redwood/gpt-4-small
```
And then sidecar logs show: `error: rpc stream closed before body` repeatedly.

sam_sre: That looks like a regression in recent sidecar change that touched streaming patches. We rolled that patch to canary ~09:40.

olivia_oncall: Decide kill-switch or rollback? Prefer minimal blast radius -> flip routing away from canary. Can we toggle feature flag to 0% canary?

nina_infra: I can flip the route policy now. Running: `routectl set-weight canary-42 0`

devops-bot: Executing: routectl set-weight canary-42 0
devops-bot: OK - canary-42 weight set to 0. New requests will drain from canary.

olivia_oncall: Good. Start draining, watch error rate. Sam, Nina, start rollback plan for the sidecar patch.

sam_sre: Initiating rollback plan. We'll patch the sidecar image to previous stable tag and roll canaries back in a controlled manner once drained. Estimated time to full drain ~2m.

incident-bot: ALERT: Error rate in us-west decreased from 12% -> 1.1% within 90s after routing change. Drops predominantly in canary pool.

matt_prodops: Notifying impacted customers of transient failures. CS: send summary to impacted trial customers.

customer-success: Acknowledged. Message queued to affected trial tenants. No enterprise customers impacted.

jessica_eng: I'm preparing the rollback manifest. Applying old sidecar image tag `sidecar:v2.1.7` to canary set.

nina_infra: Patch applied to canary nodes. Kube rolling restart in progress.

sam_sre: Watching probe status. Rolling restarts look healthy so far. If restarts continue to fail we will kill the canary pods and let normal pool handle traffic.

olivia_oncall: Hands-off (handoff) plan: If rollback completes and metrics remain normal for 10m, we'll re-enable canary at 1% and monitor. If stable, gradual ramp. If not, abort and keep traffic off canary and open a postmortem.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Rollback applied at 10:05 UTC. Probe failures resolved. Error rate back to baseline (0.4%).

jessica_eng: Confirming sidecar v2.1.7 on all canary pods. No rpc stream closed logs after restart.

matt_prodops: Recommending short blameless postmortem and a rollback playbook update. Also suggest adding alert for sudden Content-Length: 0 patterns.

sam_sre: Agreed. I'll own the postmortem. Tagging the change: `change-id: CHG-2024-11-092`.

olivia_oncall: Handoff to night oncall @sam_sre. Sam, you'll own runbook + postmortem. Status: mitigated, routing off canary, rollback applied, customers notified.

sam_sre: Taking it. Adding follow-up tasks: add unit test for streaming boundary case, add probe change to avoid false liveness triggers, update rollback checklist.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated): root cause suspected regression in sidecar streaming patch. Follow-up assigned to sam_sre.

olivia_oncall: Thanks team. If anything else pops, re-open here. :white_check_mark:
